Subject: Performance verification runbook + MAP checkpoints

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for agreeing to the extended verification window. Attached is our proposed performance verification runbook (perf_plan_v3.xlsx). High level:

- Objective: validate production SLOs for the MAP close (latency P50/P95/P99, throughput, TTFT, and behavior under burst vs steady-state concurrency).
- Test types: controlled burst ramp, long steady-state (30–60m), cold-cache TTFT, and backpressure/rate-limit sweeps.
- Metrics collected: per-request TTFT (first token), per-token latency distribution, queue length, GPU util, request rejection/429 rate, and tail latency attribution.
- Success criteria: P95 latency < 220ms for 90% of steady-state runs at target concurrency; TTFT < 400ms median on cached prompts; no more than 1% requests hitting hard-rate-limit in burst windows.

Proposed schedule (please confirm):
- Wed Apr 21 02:00-06:00 PDT: burst + steady-state runs in your staging environment (we'll coordinate instance sizing).
- Thu Apr 22 08:00-10:00 PDT: repeat with simulated production traffic patterns and our suggested rate-limit profile.

Action items before the window:
- Orchid: provide a staging endpoint with service account access and the test prompt set (we need 1k representative prompts).
- Redwood: provide Gatling load scripts (attached) and a runbook; we'll also share a live dashboard link.

If that schedule works I'll lock the MAP checkpoint dates and circulate the mutual action plan update.

Thanks —

Heads up on the test script details and what to expect:

- Warmup: we'll run a 15-minute progressive warmup at 10%, 25%, 50%, 75% of target concurrency to populate KV caches.
- Burst profile: three 90s bursts to 2x target concurrency separated by 5m cool-downs. These emulate traffic spikes we've seen in similar customers.
- Steady-state: 45-minute sustained run at target concurrency (configured in perf_plan_v3.xlsx).
- Rate-limit sweep: we'll test soft-limit thresholds (5% extra headroom) and a hard-limit policy that triggers graceful rejections (429 + Retry-After).

Notes on measurements:
- TTFT: measure at request arrival → first token emitted; cold-cache TTFT will be captured by running a separate cold-start job (no warmup).
- Queueing: Gatling probe will measure queue length at the ingress point and we'll correlate with tail latency in Grafana.

I've attached the Gatling scenarios we will run (gatling_scenarios.conf). We'll also capture raw logs to drive the MAP quality evals.

-Karthik

Subject: Re: Performance verification runbook + MAP checkpoints — initial run results

Team / Asha —

We executed the Apr 18 (dry-run) and Apr 19 controlled runs in staging. Summary highlights (full artifacts attached):

- Burst behavior: during the 2x bursts we observed queueing at the ingress; queue length peaked at ~180 concurrent requests which led to P95 token latency spikes to ~620ms (from baseline P95 ~180ms).
- Steady-state: 45m runs at target concurrency met our steady-state SLOs for CPU/GPU utilization, P95 latency averaged 210–230ms depending on prompt length.
- TTFT: cold-cache TTFT (no warmup) median = 520ms, warm-cache median = 320ms; first-token emission variance higher for prompts with long prefix encoding.
- Rate-limit behavior: our soft-limit configuration allowed graceful shedding but in bursts the soft-limit window was too wide and allowed a brief amplification. We recommend tightening the token/sec soft-limit and enabling an early-shed policy based on queue length.

Recommended immediate adjustments (for MAP checkpoint):
1) Reduce soft-rate-limit window from 10s to 4s and lower token/sec threshold by ~15% for this workload.
2) Enable prefix-aware caching for the customer prompt set to reduce TTFT variance for long-prefix prompts.
3) Add an ingress queue-length circuit breaker at 150 queued requests to trigger faster autoscaling or shed to a fallback model.

Attachments: gatling_results_20270418.zip, ttft_summary_20270418.csv

I'll also drop a Grafana snapshot to the shared Drive link. Tim — if you want to correlate with the Benchlytics sim runs I can share the raw Gatling CSVs.

—Vivek
